mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -44.9 to -36.4 over the last four weeks, indicating an established recovery trend driven by accumulating consumer activity; this momentum is expected to persist, pushing average RETAIL_REC higher over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each of the last three weeks (-44.9, -44.3, -39.4, -36.4)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's weekly value reverses and declines for two consecutive weeks following t-0w, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has been declining steadily (20.0 to 17.6). If RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points above baseline, it signals households are spending markedly less time at home, which should translate into higher discretionary RETAIL_REC visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 20.0 to 17.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL crosses below 15 but RETAIL_REC's 2-week mean does not increase relative to the prior 2-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in WORKPLACES (-39.7 to -35.1) and TRANSIT (-66.7 to -62.7) jointly indicate loosening of stay-at-home policy enforcement and resumption of commuting infrastructure use. Their combined upward co-movement is a stronger signal of broad reopening than either alone, and should drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rose each of the last two weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue rising but RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean fails to exceed the prior 4-week mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in PARKS (from -50.6 to -39.9) alongside improving TRANSIT suggests people are substituting outdoor/park-based recreation for indoor retail and recreation trips, which would suppress RETAIL_REC growth in the immediate next week even as other indicators improve.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -50.6 (t-2w) to -39.9 (t-0w) while TRANSIT also improved
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT both continue to rise but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week value also rises relative to t-0w, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-May seasonal warming typically increases outdoor park visitation independent of policy, and this seasonal pull on PARKS mobility diverts discretionary trips away from retail/recreation venues, dampening RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS values rose net over the snapshot period despite volatility
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to rise but RETAIL_REC's 2-week mean also rises relative to the prior 2-week mean, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT crosses above -60 (less negative), this marks a policy-relevant threshold indicating transit capacity restrictions have been meaningfully eased, which should unlock pent-up retail trips requiring transit access within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -60 (i.e., becomes less negative than -60)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -62.7, approaching the -60 threshold
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -60 within the horizon but RETAIL_REC's following week value does not increase relative to t-0w, the threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily normalized toward baseline (-15.3 to -6.9), reflecting reduced precautionary stockpiling behavior and growing comfort with in-person errands; this behavioral normalization is expected to generalize to other discretionary categories, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved each week from -15.3 to -6.9
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues approaching baseline but RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not increase relative to the prior 4-week mean, the normalization-spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state regime where week-over-week changes in RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES shrink to under 2 points, household routines have stabilized and further large RETAIL_REC gains are unlikely; RETAIL_REC growth should flatten rather than continue its prior rapid pace over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:week-over-week change in RESIDENTIAL narrowed to -1.1 and WORKPLACES to 1.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES week-over-week changes remain small (<2 points) but RETAIL_REC's 2-week mean rises by more than 5 points relative to the prior 2-week mean, the stabilization-flattening hypothesis is rejected.
